decision.endpoint: rank IC, h = 10, primary configuration, full universe

holm_reading.applied: t >= 3 and Holm-adjusted two-sided p <= p(t = 3)

interval_95.note: mean +/- 1.96 Newey-West s.e.; nominal and descriptive, not part of the rule

deviations_and_clarifications: **Late origins.** An origin near the end of the window is given only as many steps as there are sessions on or before 2025-09-05 after it, so no date after 2025-09-05 is used even as a calendar feature. Generation is causal, so the retained steps are what a 20-step run would have produced. The last test origin therefore has fewer than 5 steps and enters no pre-registered horizon.

**Seeds.** Path seeds are 42 + path index. So that results do not depend on batch size or device, every (origin, symbol, path) row owns a CPU generator whose 32-bit seed is the first four bytes of SHA-256 over `kronos-ic-r3/<window>/origin/<origin index>/symbol/<symbol>/path-seed/<42 + path index>`; the origin index, the path seeds and all row seeds are stored in each origin file, and the analysis recomputes the row seeds from this formula before it scores a file. Rows are sampled independently, as in upstream's batched sampler. Production runs one symbol per process and so reuses stream 42 + path for every symbol; that sharing of noise across symbols is not reproduced here. The production-configuration cells and the threshold preview therefore describe the frozen settings under independent draws, not under the exact streams the frozen books use.

**Speed-up, not a variant.** The transformer reuses cached keys and values of earlier positions instead of recomputing the context at each step, and sampling (upstream's own top-p filter, softmax and `torch.multinomial`) runs on the CPU while the transformer runs on the accelerator. The validation section gives the measured agreement with upstream.

**`t >= 3 (Holm within the horizon family)`** is applied in its stricter reading: the Newey-West t of the primary endpoint must be at least 3 and its Holm-adjusted two-sided p-value (family h = 5, 10, 20; normal reference) must not exceed the p-value of t = 3 (0.0027). That amounts to t >= 3.32 when the primary has the smallest p-value of the three, 3.21 when it has the middle one and 3.00 when it has the largest. Under the plainer reading (t >= 3 alone) a t between 3.00 and 3.32 could pass; the reading was fixed before any forecast was scored, and the decision section states whether the verdict would differ under the plainer one.

**Newey-West.** Bartlett kernel, lag = ceil(h / 5) origins, variance of the mean of the per-origin series, no small-sample correction, normal p-values. Halves are the first ceil(n / 2) and the remaining scored origins. The p-values, the Holm p-values and every 'two standard errors' statement are nominal: with this few overlapping origins they understate tail probabilities. The validation section gives the measured rejection rates when the score carries no information. The rule itself is stated on t and on the mean, and is unchanged.

**Interval in the lead.** The lead adds a nominal 95% interval (mean +/- 1.96 Newey-West standard errors) and says whether it contains zero and the paper's rank IC of 0.0622. This is a description of how tight the result is. It is not a pre-registered endpoint and takes no part in the verdict.

**Incremental regression.** Per origin, ordinary least squares with an intercept of the realised-return rank on the Kronos rank and the four simple ranks, all ranks rescaled to [-0.5, 0.5]; the coefficient series is averaged with a Newey-West t. A name without 252 earlier sessions at an origin is left out of that origin's regression and of the 252-minus-21 rank. Realised volatility is the sample standard deviation of the last 20 daily log returns. Every simple rank uses bars up to the origin only.

**Decile spreads.** A decile is floor(n / 10) names. Returns run from the open of origin + 1 to the close of origin + h. Net top-minus-bottom deducts 22 bps (a round trip on each leg); net top-minus-universe deducts 11 bps (only the top decile is traded; the universe mean is a benchmark).
**Dispersion** is the sample standard deviation across paths of the path return at h; the partial rank correlation controls for the 20-session realised-volatility rank.

**Memorisation flag.** 'More than two standard errors' is read as two standard errors of the difference, sqrt(se_contrast^2 + se_test^2), with Newey-West standard errors. The contrast universe additionally requires every session from 2022-06-01. Contrast origins are scored by the same rule as test origins (origin + h on or before 2025-09-05), so a few of the latest contrast targets fall after June 2024; the count is given below. The flag compares two different market periods and fires on the gap alone, so the report also says whether the contrast-window IC is itself positive.
**Snapshot-11 subset** means study-universe members that are complete members of data snapshot 11 (every XNYS session 2016-10-17 to 2025-09-05 in `massive` bars).
**Threshold preview** uses steps 5 and 20 of the single 20-step generation of the production configuration.
**`amount`** is volume x mean(open, high, low, close), the value upstream fills in when, as in production, no amount column is supplied.

**Device check G0** compares the softmax of the first-step logits of both token heads (at T = 1 and at the sampling temperature) between CPU and the accelerator; the distribution after the top-p filter and every later step are also recorded in the check's output.

**Pilot origin.** The first test origin (2024-07-01) was generated during the throughput pilot and kept, because the run is resumable. It was made by the same version of the script as every other origin (the run cannot be resumed by a different one). Its forecasts were not compared with realised returns before this analysis.

**Production configuration before the primary run.** The pre-registration says the secondary configuration runs only after the primary finishes, and the script refuses the secondary run until then. Before the primary run, the production configuration was nevertheless used for validation: the device check on 32 series and the three-symbol equivalence check (each run once when the scripts were built and once more after the review repairs), the code review's own comparison of 24 production-configuration paths with upstream, and one full-size origin that the first pilot timed without saving it and without leaving a log. No forecast from any of these was kept or compared with realised returns.

**Review repairs before the run.** After two adversarial reviews and before the long run, the scripts were hardened: a real look-ahead test, the script hash frozen into the run definition and stored in every origin file, stricter checks of every origin file at scoring time, a 20:00 UTC cut-off, distinct exit codes, no scoring of incomplete runs, and the wording and tables of this report. The sampling code was not changed (its syntax tree is identical before and after), and the pilot origin regenerated by the final script is bitwise identical to the first one; the validation section gives the records.

**Look-ahead.** No bar after an origin can enter its input because the input is cut from a view that ends at the origin. That is true by construction, so it is tested from outside: for every origin the input is rebuilt with all later bars replaced by NaN and must be bit-for-bit identical, and an input deliberately cut one session late must be caught.
**Rank IC at every generated horizon** is shown for completeness. Only h = 5, 10 and 20 are pre-registered endpoints; the other horizons are descriptive and carry no adjustment.
**Incomplete runs are not scored.** The analysis refuses an incomplete primary run outright. An incomplete secondary or contrast run is reported as incomplete and none of its forecasts is read.
